analytical_question: What innovation does the proposed application represent, what value could it create or displace, and which business-model judgment is defensible for the specified organization?
general_et_finding: Agentic AI combines LLM reasoning with tool use and feedback [S2]. Its development includes invention, practical innovation and commercial offerings [S3, C1]; these dimensions overlap. Availability is not proof of vendor profitability or market-wide diffusion. The supplied evidence does not establish a universal breakthrough against existing automation. This technology-level conclusion stays unchanged across the cases.

evidence.claim: Innovation requires meaningful difference and implementation; organizational novelty need not be world novelty.
evidence.notes: A specific SPS deployment or a universal breakthrough threshold.

evidence.claim: Separates model-directed tool use from fixed workflows; discusses complexity and compounding errors.
evidence.notes: Independent proof of superiority, reliability or savings at SPS; current tooling completeness.

evidence.claim: Commercial availability of an enterprise agent offering was announced in 2024.
evidence.notes: Verified customer ROI, broad adoption, current price, or SPS procurement.

evidence.claim: Public admissions information and staff appointment channels exist.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S4] NYU School of Professional Studies, Graduate Admissions. https://www.sps.nyu.edu/join/graduate-admissions.html
evidence.notes: Internal CRM, response delays, staff costs, AI deployment, lost applicants, or adoption posture.

evidence.claim: A pre-LLM conversational assistant was tested for pre-enrollment support at Georgia State.
evidence.source_or_reference: [S5] Lindsay C. Page and Hunter Gehlbach, How an Artificially Intelligent Virtual Assistant Helps Students Navigate the Road to College. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/pdf/10.1177/2332858417749220
evidence.notes: Agentic-LLM superiority, NYU graduate applicant results, or transfer of effect sizes.

evidence.claim: The course separates sustaining/disruptive logic and business exposure by severity and time horizon.
evidence.source_or_reference: [C2] Andres Fortino, ET Creative Destruction FA26 (2).pptx, slides 9 and 24; user-supplied course material.
evidence.notes: Framework only. The numerical planning bins and scenario placements are analytical choices, not observed outcomes.

application_finding: Status: unimplemented proposal. The described FAQ assistant has fixed retrieval and no model-directed tool/action loop, so it does not instantiate agentic AI under the working definition [S2]. General technology evidence remains unchanged. Whether the local design is an innovation is unresolved: it might improve access significantly or merely reproduce the existing FAQ. There is no implemented local breakthrough [S1, C1].
organization_specific_finding: Business-Model Disruption Judgment: Insufficient evidence. Target: SPS routine information support; horizon: the stated 12 months. No current baseline or economic comparison justifies even a Low score. A conditional Low/sustaining scenario would be reasonable only if the design adds convenience while leaving the offer, revenue logic, channel control and advantage substantially unchanged. Possible creation is easier access; possible displacement is some repetitive search and drafting. The magnitude, beneficiaries and review burden are not established. Withhold a position on the severity/time matrix [C2] until the baseline and likely timing are documented.
contrary_evidence_or_limitations: A non-agentic tool can still be a useful organizational innovation. The architecture finding must not be treated as proof of no value.
A large verified accessibility or service improvement could change the local assessment, while equivalent results from the current FAQ would support routine improvement or no material innovation.
No evidence establishes a new-market foothold, a revenue-model change or displacement of an intermediary.
confidence_and_uncertainty: High confidence in the architecture mismatch because the case explicitly excludes agent-directed tools. Insufficient evidence for local innovation status, disruption severity or timing.
value_opportunity_implication: Test convenience and staff support without attributing benefit to autonomy that is absent from the design.
risk_governance_implication: Fluent answers can still be wrong. Counselor review does not prove zero risk, and the agent label should not justify new permissions. The early-versus-late adoption tradeoff remains unresolved without measured incremental value.
recommendation_management_implication: Request the actual before/after workflow, implementation status and task results. Compare this simpler proposal directly with the primary agent candidate. Adoption and Readiness assess suitability; Landscape checks alternatives, Diffusion checks uptake and Promethean handles wider significance. Do not manufacture a disruption rating.
change_monitoring_triggers: Proposed owner: workflow owner. Supply baseline and proposed steps; if the difference is only wording, withhold an innovation label. Meaningful use and demonstrated difference could justify a local innovation finding.

Proposed owner: admissions quality and finance. Compare cost per correctly completed support task, including review, integration, platform, monitoring and correction, with the existing FAQ/staff process. Use the results to set a defensible severity and timing judgment.
Proposed owner: technical lead. If model-directed tools and actions are actually added, rerun the architecture classification and permission review; a marketing rename alone changes nothing.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Actual baseline, implementation evidence, economic data and time-to-change evidence are required.
No unconditional innovation, breakthrough, disruption-level or adoption conclusion is issued.
